paras: The lynching of Theodore Burton was the hanging of a jailed man by fifty masked men near Belgreene, Alabama, reported in a Montgomery dispatch dated February 23, 1882. Burton, accused of killing John Rockard with an axe, was taken from jail after the men forced the sheriff to give up the keys, and his body was found hanging from a tree the next morning. Northern dailies printed the dispatch as the lynching of a "desperado" or "murderer," and weekly crime digests carried a brief version into March.

According to the dispatch, Burton and Rockard were splitting rails near Belgreene when they fell into a "feud," and Burton killed Rockard with two blows of an axe and fled. Four men, named as Eugene Dobbs, James and William Dempsey, and a Mr. Bushfield, captured him. While the party stopped to rest on the way back, Burton reportedly drew a bowie knife, badly wounded two of his captors and escaped again, but he was recaptured and placed in jail.

That night fifty masked men entered the town and compelled the sheriff to surrender the jail keys. The Omaha Daily Bee's version adds that they went to the sheriff's house and demanded the keys of both the jail and the "cage" in which the prisoner was held. The men took Burton out, put him on a horse and "quietly rode away" with him to a spot three-quarters of a mile south of the town, where they hanged him from a tree. His body was found there the next morning.

The coverage does not name any of the masked men, and no report of an inquest, arrests or official inquiry into the lynching was found. None of the reports gives the race of Burton, Rockard or the lynchers.

The story reached Northern papers on February 24 in two wordings of the same Montgomery dispatch. The Lancaster Daily Intelligencer and the Wilmington Daily Republican headlined it "A Desperado Lynched" and referred to Burton as "the murderer," treating the accusation as settled. The Omaha Daily Bee ran its version as "MURDERER LYNCHED" in a column of crime news, giving the names as "Q. H. Barton" and "John Rookard" and the place as "Bellegreen." None of these papers commented on the lynching itself.

A week later the item circulated as a one-paragraph brief in weekly crime digests, under headings such as "Tragical Tales" and "Crimes and Criminals," in the Mower County Transcript in Minnesota and the Hand County Press in Dakota. The same briefs appeared in the Watertown Republican and Superior Times in Wisconsin and the Crawford Avalanche in Michigan between March 1 and March 4. These condensations renamed the men "T. H. Burton" and "John Packard," and one version reduced the captors to "three citizens" and the wounded to one. No report from an Alabama paper was found in the coverage.

The reports differ on names and small details rather than on the core events: the victim appears as Theodore Burton, Q. H. Barton or T. H. Burton, and the dead man as Rockard, Rookard or Packard. The Mower County Transcript dated the killing of Packard "on the 23d," the date of the Montgomery dispatch, while the fuller February 24 reports give no calendar date for either the killing or the hanging.

reader.title: Lynching of Theodore Burton
chips: Lynching of any race (not in the anti-Black count)
bases: A band of fifty masked men took a jailed man accused of murder from the jail at night and hanged him from a tree outside the town (A1, A2, A3).

Fifty masked men forced the sheriff to give up the jail keys, took the prisoner and hanged him, so he was killed without lawful authority by a group well over three (A1, A2, A3); they acted on the accusation that he had killed John Rockard, a pretext of justice (A1, A3).
Every report traces to one Montgomery dispatch of Feb. 23, printed in two wordings (A1, A2; A3) and later condensed into digest briefs (A5, A6); no local Alabama report or follow-up was found.

accounts.label: Montgomery wire dispatch (first wording)
accounts.gist: Theodore Burton killed John Rockard in a feud, was captured, wounded two captors, was recaptured and jailed; fifty masked men forced the sheriff to give up the keys, rode off with him, and his body was found hanging from a tree the next morning.

accounts.label: Montgomery dispatch (National Associated Press column wording)
accounts.gist: The same story with the names 'Q. H. Barton', 'John Rookard' and 'Bellegreen', adding that the men went to the sheriff's house for the keys of the jail and the cage, and hanged him three-fourths of a mile south.

accounts.label: Weekly digest briefs
accounts.gist: Condensed versions naming 'T. H. Burton' and 'John Packard'; one says three citizens captured him and dates the killing 'on the 23d'.

framing.detail: Printed the dispatch under 'A Desperado Lynched', calling Burton 'the murderer' and stating the accusation as fact, with no comment on the lynching.
The Omaha Bee ran its version as 'MURDERER LYNCHED' in a column of crime dispatches.
Weekly papers in Minnesota, Dakota, Wisconsin and Michigan carried a one-paragraph brief in crime digests ('Tragical Tales', 'Crimes and Criminals').

conflicts.note: Variants of one name in copies of the same dispatch; the same captors and acts appear in each, so one man is meant.
A5 is a later condensation; the fuller Feb. 24 dispatches (A1, A3) are the better evidence.

versions.value: Dispatch dated Feb. 23; lynching at night, body found next morning

conflicts.note: A5's date appears to take the dispatch date as the date of the killing; the dispatch itself gives no calendar dates for the killing or the hanging.

record_check.dossier: One victim, Theodore Burton; 'Q. H. Barton' and 'T. H. Burton' are variants of his name in other copies of the dispatch.
Montgomery is only the dateline; the masked men entered 'the town' where Burton was jailed, near Belgreene, and hanged him three-quarters of a mile south of it.

record_check.record: ...took Theodore Burton, who had been captured after killing John Rockard
record_check.dossier: He was accused of killing Rockard; the reports state it as fact but no trial or inquest is reported. He was captured, wounded two captors in an escape attempt, and was recaptured before being jailed.
Date of the Montgomery dispatch; the hanging occurred on or shortly before that date, at night, but no paper gives its calendar date.
No county is named in any report.

info: Reported in a Montgomery dispatch dated Feb. 23, 1882; the lynching took place at night and the body was found the next morning, but no paper gives the calendar date of the hanging. One digest dates the killing of Packard [Rockard] 'on the 23d'.
Near Belgreene ('Bellegreen' in A3), Alabama; the prisoner was held in the town jail and hanged from a tree three-quarters of a mile south of the town.
One man, named 'Theodore Burton' (A1, A2), 'Q. H. Barton' (A3) or 'T. H. Burton' (A5, A6); race not stated.

Accused of killing John Rockard ('John Rookard', 'John Packard') with two blows of an axe after a feud while splitting rails, and of badly wounding two of his captors with a bowie knife while trying to escape.
Unidentified masked men; no names, race or organization given.
